attrs.citation: J. P. Anderson, Computer Security Technology Planning Study, ESD-TR-73-51 (1972) — the reference monitor concept; the NEAT criteria as later stated
hypotheses: the mechanism mediates a defined subject/object/operation relation — the requirements are stated relative to that relation and say nothing outside it
attrs.note: The word to keep is EVALUABLE. Anderson's list already concedes that non-bypassability is discharged by evaluation of the mechanism — analysis, verification, review — and not by the mechanism reporting on itself. That is why R7.3 splits GPT-5.6's single law: the always-invoked half is checkable at admission, the non-bypassable half is an evaluation obligation.
attrs.result: A reference validation mechanism must be Non-bypassable, Evaluable and Always-invoked, and must additionally be tamperproof. These are DESIGN REQUIREMENTS on a mechanism, not properties a mechanism can test of itself.
